Answer: C
Reason: The frontal view (Figure 5a) shows the opacity projecting over the mid-thoracic spine, and the lateral view (Figure 5b) confirms it is located posteriorly at the level of the vertebral bodies rather than within the lung parenchyma. This specific location and appearance are characteristic of a pseudo rib articulation (often between the 6th and 7th ribs), which is a common benign anatomical variant that can mimic a lung nodule on frontal imaging.
